english: Let $b$ and $c$ be real numbers and let $P:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $P(x)=3x^{2}+bx+c$. Then
hindi: माना कि $b$ तथा $c$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं और $P:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $P(x)=3x^{2}+bx+c$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब
solution: For a quadratic the second difference is constant: $P(n+2)-2P(n+1)+P(n)=2\cdot3=6$
$b$ and $c$ drop out: for the linear part $bx+c$ alone the rows satisfy $R_1+R_3=2R_2$, so it contributes nothing
solution_full: Apply $R_3\to R_3-2R_2+R_1$ (value unchanged, since a multiple of other rows is added). The new third row is $(u_2-2u_1+u_0,\ u_3-2u_2+u_1,\ u_4-2u_3+u_2)=(6,6,6)$.
Apply $R_2\to R_2-R_1$. The new second row is $(u_1-u_0,\ u_2-u_1,\ u_3-u_2)=(3+b,\ 9+b,\ 15+b)$. The first row stays $(c,\ 3+b+c,\ 12+2b+c)$.
Apply $C_2\to C_2-C_1$: the second column becomes $(3+b,\ 6,\ 0)$.
Apply $C_3\to C_3-2C_2+C_1$ (using the original second column): first row $12+2b+c-2(3+b+c)+c=6$, second row $15+b-2(9+b)+(3+b)=0$, third row $6-12+6=0$.
Why $b$ and $c$ do not matter: if $P$ were linear, $u_{n+2}-2u_{n+1}+u_n=0$, so $R_3=2R_2-R_1$ and the determinant is $0$; only the $x^{2}$ part survives, and it gives $-8\cdot3^{3}=-216$.
Option (D) is the value $-4\cdot 27$ obtained by forgetting the factor $2$ in the second difference.
originality_note: New: the Hankel determinant of the values of a quadratic at 0,...,4 is independent of the linear and constant coefficients, which the student must discover through second differences (way 4: hidden invariant). Closest known: determinants whose rows are in AP, or with entries of an AP. Different because: the entries are values of an unknown quadratic, the rows are not in AP, and the answer depends only on the leading coefficient.
blueprint_concepts: Determinant when a row is a linear combination of the others

concept_use.Application of properties of determinant: Row and column operations R3-2R2+R1, R2-R1, C3-2C2+C1, C2-C1 reduce the determinant to a triangular-type form.
concept_use.Determinant when a row is a linear combi: For the linear part bx+c the third row equals 2R2-R1, so that part contributes zero; this is why b and c drop out.

stem_review: Read as a student: b, c real and P defined on R; determinant written in full; one reading. Checked with sympy that the value is -216 for symbolic b, c. Answer at (C) as planned; options all numbers. Changed: No change.
key_step: Second differences of a quadratic are constant, so R3-2R2+R1 is a constant row and b, c disappear.
justification: Routine chain of row and column operations once the second-difference idea is seen; no unfamiliar idea, but three or four steps. Comparable to 2025-P1-Q1 (L2), coefficient extraction for polynomials.
